title: Dumpster Rental CRM: 6 Tools That Stop Quotes Going Cold
html:
A dumpster rental CRM only has to do one thing well: make sure no call or quote request goes cold. HubSpot and Zoho both offer a free plan, Jobber and Housecall Pro add pipeline tools to scheduling, and Calendly handles online booking. Pick one place to log every lead, then connect it to your marketing and the dumpster rental marketing that brings the calls in. Paid plans in this guide run from $10 to $299 a month.

A dumpster rental CRM is a shared notebook for every person who ever asked for a container. Most yards keep that notebook in a phone, a whiteboard and a dispatcher's memory. This guide covers six tools that replace it, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

The money in dumpster rental is in repeat customers. A roofer who rents one container will rent again next month, and a homeowner who had a good drop will tell a neighbor. A CRM keeps the address, the container size, the last price and the next follow-up in one record, so the second order takes two minutes instead of ten.

Which dumpster rental CRM is free to start with?

HubSpot and Zoho CRM both publish a free plan, and either is enough to log leads for a small yard. Neither knows what a roll-off is, so you add your own fields.

  • HubSpot CRM: a contact and deal tracker with email sync. The Free plan covers up to 2 users and 1,000 contacts with no time limit, and the Starter plan lists a $20 per seat list price, with a new customer discount of $10 per seat month to month. Limit: Free has 2,000 email sends a month with HubSpot branding, so it suits tracking more than marketing.
  • Zoho CRM: a deal pipeline with custom fields and reports. The Free edition covers up to 3 users. Limit: the Free edition allows 10 custom email templates, 10 data exports and 5,000 API calls a day, and paid prices appear in your local currency, so check the vendor for a dollar figure.

Add the fields a rental needs: container size, drop address, drop date, expected pickup date, customer type and lead source. Homeowner and contractor accounts behave differently, so tag them from day one. A contractor with three jobs a month deserves a call before the customer who rented once.

Start in the free plan and only pay when a limit stops you. A yard that never emails more than a few hundred people will not hit the 2,000 send cap. A yard with five dispatchers will hit the user caps fast.

Which tools follow up quotes and bookings for a dumpster company?

Jobber and Housecall Pro both pair scheduling with a sales pipeline, and Calendly adds simple online booking. Pick the one that matches how customers contact you.

  • Jobber: its site says it lets customers request work, approve quotes and receive automated quote follow-ups. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Limit: Pipeline is a $49 a month add-on, and extra users cost $29 a month each.
  • Housecall Pro: Basic is $59 a month billed annually for one user, and Essentials is $149 a month billed annually for 5 users. Limit: Pipeline, Campaigns and Voice are listed as add-ons without prices.
  • Calendly: lets a customer pick a time for a call or site visit. Free has one event type and one calendar connection, and Standard is listed at $10 per seat a month. Limit: it books a time, but it does not hold deal history.

Speed beats polish in this trade. A person looking for a container usually calls two or three yards in a row. The yard that answers and sends a clear quote first often wins the order. Whatever tool you choose, set a rule that every quote request gets a reply within the hour during business hours.

Zoho CRMCustom pipelineFree for 3 usersPrices in local currency
JobberQuotes and follow-up$49 monthly, $29 annualPipeline add-on $49
Housecall ProScheduling and pipeline$59 annual, $79 monthlyAdd-ons unpriced
CalendlyOnline bookingFree, then $10 a seatOne event type on Free
DocketRoll-off dispatch and CRM linksNot publishedOne-year agreement

Prices checked on each vendor page in November 2026. Annual prices are per month billed yearly.

Can dispatch software double as a dumpster rental CRM?

Partly. Docket is built for roll-off dispatch, and its Pro plan adds integrations and a review tool. It is not a full sales CRM.

  • Docket: its published plans lists Grow, Pro and Pro Plus, billed monthly per truck with office staff free. Pro adds Local SEO, integrations with Mailchimp, Samsara, Verizon Connect and Dumpsters.com, and Review Guard. Limit: prices are not published, and the page states a one-year agreement.

The question is where customer history should live. If your dispatch tool keeps the order and the address, it is the system of record for jobs. A CRM then only needs the lead before it becomes a job. Pick one source for each fact and write down which it is, so two people never edit the same phone number in two places.

This guide stays on leads and follow-up. Dispatch, routing and billing belong to a separate tool, so keep that choice apart from the CRM choice.

What should a dumpster rental CRM track?

A dumpster rental CRM should track the facts that change a price or a schedule. Everything else is noise.

  • Contact and account type: name, phone, email and whether it is a homeowner or a contractor account.
  • Job details: drop address, container size, material type and any placement notes such as a gate code.
  • Dates: requested drop date, expected pickup date and the date of the last contact.
  • Lead source: map listing, search ad, referral or repeat customer, so you know what is paying for itself.
  • Status: new, quoted, booked, delivered, picked up and lost, with a reason for each lost lead.

Lead source is the field most yards skip. Without it you cannot tell whether your map listing or your search ads brought the call. Ask every caller how they found you and enter the answer. Ten calls a week for a month give you a usable pattern.

How do you set up a dumpster lead pipeline?

Use five stages and one rule for each. A pipeline with ten stages never gets updated.

  • New: every call, form or booking request lands here the same day.
  • Quoted: the customer has a written price. Follow up once the next day and once after three days.
  • Booked: a drop date is set, and the job moves to dispatch.
  • Completed: the container is picked up, the invoice is out and a review request goes with it.
  • Lost: the customer chose someone else or the date passed. Log the reason, such as price or timing.

Review requests belong in the last step. Google states that creating a Business Profile is free, and reviews on that profile help the next caller choose you.

A CRM only stores leads. Rankings from dumpster rental SEO and paid clicks from dumpster rental Google Ads create them.

What mistakes do dumpster yards make with a CRM?

Most CRM failures come from habits, not software. Five mistakes show up again and again in small yards.

  • Two sources of truth: leads live in the CRM, but the dispatcher keeps a paper list too. Pick one and retire the other within a week.
  • Too many fields: a form with twenty required fields gets skipped on a busy Monday. Require five and make the rest optional.
  • No owner: if nobody is named to update the pipeline, nobody does. Assign one person and give that person a daily ten minute check.
  • No lost reason: a lost lead with no reason teaches you nothing. Even a short note such as price or date helps you adjust.
  • Paying for add-ons early: pipeline, campaigns and voice tools cost extra at Jobber and Housecall Pro. Use the basics for a month, then buy only what you miss.

A short weekly review keeps the system honest. Each Friday, open the quoted stage and call every lead older than three days. Then count how many booked jobs came from each source. Fifteen minutes a week is enough to catch a stalled lead before a competitor books it.

Think about contractor accounts separately. A roofer or remodeler who rents containers all season is worth a standing price and a direct phone number. Tag those accounts, note their usual container size and set a reminder to check in before their busy months. That kind of follow-up costs nothing and is rarely done.

Missed calls deserve their own rule. If the office is busy or closed, a lead can slip away in the time it takes to find a pen. Jobber lists an AI Receptionist add-on at $29 a month, Housecall Pro lists a Voice add-on without a price, and Docket lists messaging in its Grow plan. Test any of them with a real after-hours call before you rely on it, and write down who checks the voicemail each morning.

How do you choose a dumpster rental CRM?

Choose a dumpster rental CRM with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Test each tool against the same ten recent leads before you commit.

Fit: can it hold container size, drop date and account type, and can dispatchers see the notes?

Cost: add the plan, extra users and add-ons such as pipeline or marketing tools, then compare against one average rental.

Setup effort: can you import your customer list and build the five stages in one afternoon?

A one-person office fits a free plan from HubSpot or Zoho with Calendly Free. A yard with two dispatchers who quote all day fits Jobber or Housecall Pro, which keep scheduling and follow-up together. A roll-off fleet already on Docket should ask what its integrations connect to before it buys a second tool.

Whichever route you take, load your last 50 customers first and call five of them. That one afternoon shows you whether the tool is easy enough for the whole team to use.

What is the best CRM for a dumpster rental company?

A small yard can start on the HubSpot or Zoho free plan. A yard that quotes all day may prefer Jobber or Housecall Pro because scheduling and follow-up sit together.

Is there a free CRM for dumpster rental businesses?

Yes. HubSpot lists a Free plan for up to 2 users with 1,000 contacts, and Zoho CRM lists a Free edition for up to 3 users. Both have caps on email, templates or exports, so check each limit before you rely on it.

Does Jobber have a CRM for dumpster rentals?

Jobber describes a field service CRM with quote requests, approvals and automated follow-ups. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment. Pipeline is a separate add-on at $49 a month, and extra users cost $29 a month each.

What lead sources should a dumpster rental CRM track?

Track map listing, search ads, referrals, repeat contractors and walk-ins. Ask every caller how they found you and enter the answer as a field. After a month you can see which source brings booked jobs, not just calls, and shift effort there.

How fast should a dumpster company reply to a quote request?

Reply within the hour during business hours. Customers often contact several yards at once and choose the first clear quote. Set a rule in your CRM that flags any new request without a reply, so no lead waits overnight by accident.

Cost:
add the plan, extra users and add-ons such as pipeline or marketing tools, then compare against one average rental.
Setup effort:
can you import your customer list and build the five stages in one afternoon?
A one-person office fits a free plan from HubSpot or Zoho with Calendly Free. A yard with two dispatchers who quote all day fits Jobber or Housecall Pro, which keep scheduling and follow-up together. A roll-off fleet already on Docket should ask what its integrations connect to before it buys a second tool.
Whichever route you take, load your last 50 customers first and call five of them. That one afternoon shows you whether the tool is easy enough for the whole team to use.
###
What is the best CRM for a dumpster rental company?
A small yard can start on the HubSpot or Zoho free plan. A yard that quotes all day may prefer Jobber or Housecall Pro because scheduling and follow-up sit together.
###
Is there a free CRM for dumpster rental businesses?
Yes. HubSpot lists a Free plan for up to 2 users with 1,000 contacts, and Zoho CRM lists a Free edition for up to 3 users. Both have caps on email, templates or exports, so check each limit before you rely on it.
###
Does Jobber have a CRM for dumpster rentals?
Jobber describes a field service CRM with quote requests, approvals and automated follow-ups. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment. Pipeline is a separate add-on at $49 a month, and extra users cost $29 a month each.
###
What lead sources should a dumpster rental CRM track?
Track map listing, search ads, referrals, repeat contractors and walk-ins. Ask every caller how they found you and enter the answer as a field. After a month you can see which source brings booked jobs, not just calls, and shift effort there.
###
How fast should a dumpster company reply to a quote request?
Reply within the hour during business hours. Customers often contact several yards at once and choose the first clear quote. Set a rule in your CRM that flags any new request without a reply, so no lead waits overnight by accident.
